holidays.name: National Day of the Gong
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the gong, a big, shimmering metal disc that can sound like thunder or like a lullaby. Fans are encouraged to attend a gong performance, listen to the different gong styles, or take part in a sound bath where the gong is the star.
holidays.origin: The observance was created to honor the gong's place in music, ceremony, creativity, and healing. It was authorized as an annual June 21 observance in 2017.
holidays.funFact: A gong's pitch changes with its size and shape, and a single strike can ring and swell for a long time. That makes it one of the few instruments that seems to get louder after you've stopped playing it.

holidays.name: Go Skateboarding Day
holidays.description: Skaters around the world grab their boards and roll out to celebrate. Parks, plazas, and sidewalks fill up with kickflips, cruising, and a few unplanned bails. Beginners are welcome to try it too.
holidays.origin: The International Association of Skateboard Companies founded this observance in 2004. It is held every year on the summer solstice date of June 21.
holidays.funFact: The holiday falls on the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, so skaters get the most daylight possible for a session.

holidays.name: National Selfie Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the self-portrait. Strike a pose, find your best angle, and share the results with the world. Group selfies, silly faces, and photos with pets all count.
holidays.origin: The day recognizes the smartphone and social media phenomenon of sharing self-portraits online. It is an unofficial observance that is listed on June 21 each year.
holidays.funFact: Oxford Dictionaries named "selfie" its Word of the Year in 2013, after use of the word jumped by thousands of percent in a single year.
